skill.name: markdown
skill.description: Markdown linting and automated fixing for documentation files using markdownlint-cli2. It guides agents through checks, safe fixes, manual cleanup, configuration, and final reporting.
skill.summary: Lint, fix, and validate Markdown documents with markdownlint-cli2 guidance.
skill.author: 46ki75

security_audit.summary: The static analyzer matched Markdown fences and inline code as Ruby backtick execution. Review found documented markdownlint-cli2 usage and a public documentation URL, with no prompt injection, data exfiltration, or arbitrary command construction in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Broad auto-fix examples can modify many Markdown files when used without scope confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to confirm target paths before running recursive or multi-file auto-fix commands.

remediation.issue: Command examples do not explicitly mention safe handling of user-provided file paths.
remediation.suggestion: Add a note to quote or validate paths before passing them to shell commands.

content.value_statement: Markdown files often drift from project style rules and become harder to maintain. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through markdownlint-cli2 checks, fixes, and clear reporting.
actual_capabilities: Guides markdownlint-cli2 auto-fix runs for one or more Markdown files.
Checks remaining Markdown lint errors after automated formatting.
Explains common markdownlint rules such as heading levels, long lines, and code fences.
Applies manual cleanup guidance for issues auto-fix cannot resolve.
Helps create or adjust markdownlint configuration for project needs.
Summarizes initial errors, automated fixes, manual edits, and final validation results.
limitations: Requires markdownlint-cli2 to be installed in the execution environment.
Can modify files when auto-fix is used, so changes should be reviewed.
Cannot infer every project writing convention without user guidance.
Does not validate rendered output, links, or factual accuracy beyond lint rules.

use_cases.title: Clean Pull Request Documentation
use_cases.description: Lint README updates, fix common style issues, and report what changed before review.

use_cases.title: Standardize Documentation Sets
use_cases.description: Apply consistent markdownlint rules across guides, tutorials, and reference pages.

use_cases.title: Prepare User-Facing Guides
use_cases.description: Find heading, spacing, and formatting issues before publishing Markdown content.

prompt_templates.title: Check One File
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner validation of a single Markdown document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this Markdown file for lint issues. Explain the main problems and suggest safe fixes before changing it.

prompt_templates.title: Auto-Fix and Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Routine cleanup for a draft or README.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the Markdown auto-fix workflow on this file, then report the initial errors, remaining issues, and final result.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Manual Lint Issues
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate cleanup after auto-fix leaves structural problems.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the remaining markdownlint errors. Fix heading hierarchy, emphasis-as-heading, and line wrapping issues while preserving meaning.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Project Rules
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced configuration for a repository with custom style rules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this project documentation style. Propose a markdownlint configuration and apply it to the selected files with a change summary.

output_examples.input: A README has multiple top-level headings and inconsistent blank lines.
output: The report lists the initial lint errors and the rules involved.
The final summary says which headings were adjusted and confirms a clean lint result.

output_examples.input: An API guide needs consistent line length and code block language labels.
output: The guide is reformatted where safe, with unresolved style decisions called out clearly.
The summary separates automatic fixes from manual edits for easier review.

output_examples.input: A legacy document uses embedded HTML and long URLs.
output_examples.output: The result recommends a project-specific configuration and explains which rules should stay enabled or disabled.

best_practices: Run lint checks before and after edits so the final state is clear.
Review auto-fix changes when files contain generated content or complex examples.
Use a project configuration when documentation intentionally differs from default rules.
anti_patterns: Running broad auto-fix commands across a repository without confirming scope.
Disabling lint rules globally when only one document needs an exception.
Changing document hierarchy only to satisfy lint rules without checking meaning.

faq.question: What does this skill use to lint Markdown?
faq.answer: It uses markdownlint-cli2 guidance to check files, apply safe fixes, and verify the result.

faq.question: Can it automatically fix every lint issue?
faq.answer: No. Heading structure, emphasis used as headings, and long lines often need human judgment.

faq.question: Does it require local tooling?
faq.answer: Yes. The environment must have markdownlint-cli2 available for command-based linting.

faq.question: Can it work with custom markdownlint rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide configuration changes for project rules such as line length and allowed HTML.

faq.question: Will it preserve document meaning?
faq.answer: It aims to preserve meaning, but structural edits should be reviewed for important documents.

faq.question: Is it useful for generated documentation?
faq.answer: Yes, but generated files may need relaxed rules or exclusions to avoid unwanted churn.
